references.role: exact in-game rabbit-worker identity, clothing, proportions, palette, outline, and lighting
existing directional push-pose study for hand placement and forward lean

common_prompt: Create an eight-pose walk cycle of the same rabbit pushing an unseen pallet jack. Both gloved hands stay together at a fixed waist-level handle grip with a slight forward lean. Do not draw the jack, handle, ground, shadow, or other object. Create an RGBA atlas with exactly eight equal 384x512 cells in a 4-column by 2-row row-major layout on a 1536x1024 canvas. Poses are left-foot contact, left weight-down, right foot passing, right knee-up, right-foot contact, right weight-down, left passing, left knee-up. Make every pose visibly distinct with alternating feet. Keep one complete character at consistent scale with at least 24 transparent pixels from every cell edge. Match the softer textured in-game sprite style, preserve clothing and toolbelt side, and avoid clipping, duplicated poses, detached parts, extra limbs, halos, matte, checkerboard, text, borders, watermark, and pallet-jack parts.

east.additional_prompt: Keep this exact side-facing view; keep the toolbelt on the same side and both hands on the implied handle.

north.view: due north, directly away from the camera; rear view

northeast.view: northeast three-quarter rear view, facing upper-right

southeast.view: southeast three-quarter front view, facing lower-right

south.view: due south, directly toward the camera; front view

normalization.method: non-destructive cell extraction and canvas placement
normalization.mirror_policy: east, northeast, and southeast source views mirror for west, northwest, and southwest
